clue.text: Arithmetician clocks on for this time

definitions.meaning: one who adds figures together, a person who sums
the season when British clocks are put forward an hour

explanation.definitionFit: A calculator who totals numbers can whimsically be called one who sums, and the warm season is when daylight saving moves clocks forward.

clue.text: Flagging energy no bar to such-communication

definitions.text: Flagging energy no bar to such-communication

parts.words: Flagging energy no bar to such-communication
parts.note: flagging is read literally as signalling with flags, a visual message system that a tired sender can still use

explanation.surface: Even when tired you can still send this kind of message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flagging' seems to mean tiring, but it is also waving flags: the clue says signalling with flags is the communication meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The system of signalling with two hand-held flags in set positions sends letters visually.

clue.text: High spot of the muezzin's calling

definitions.text: High spot of the muezzin's calling

parts.words: High spot of the muezzin's calling
parts.note: the high place a muezzin calls the faithful to prayer from, while also seeming to mean the peak of his career

explanation.surface: The best moment in the career of a mosque's prayer-caller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' looks like vocation and 'high spot' like the peak, but it is the tall tower from which the call to prayer is literally made.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender tower attached to a mosque is where the call to prayer is given.

clue.text: Zealous type sat in the US Assembly

indicators.note: assembly means putting parts together, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A keen activist had a seat in an American legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembly' looks like a legislature but signals rearranging the letters of SAT IN THE US.
explanation.definitionFit: A passionately keen fan or devotee is full of zeal for their interest.

clue.text: Stingy type unwelcome once in glass houses?

definitions.meaning: a creature with a sting in its tail
an ancient siege engine that hurled stones, and people in glass houses should not throw stones

explanation.surface: A mean person was never welcome among those who live in glasshouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stingy' suggests meanness but means having a sting. The second half plays on the proverb 'people in glass houses shouldn't throw stones': a Roman stone-throwing catapult had the same name as the arachnid.
explanation.definitionFit: The arachnid carries a venomous sting, and the Roman catapult shared its name, a stone-hurler no greenhouse owner would welcome.

clue.text: Type of punishment has point for some showing stripes

parts.note: corporal punishment is physical punishment
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Some form of punishment involving a point leaves people striped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripes' suggests weals from a beating, but they are rank stripes on a uniform sleeve: two for these soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Army non-commissioned officers of this rank wear two chevrons on the arm.

clue.text: Talk wildly of Poe's tail-less bird

indicators.note: a bird without its tail loses its final letter

parts.note: the raven, specifically Poe's, from his poem The Raven

explanation.surface: Ranting about a bird from an Edgar Allan Poe poem that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Allan Poe wrote the poem The Raven, so 'of Poe's' points to that bird; tail-less, it loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak incoherently or with frenzied enthusiasm is to rant.

clue.text: Bill on form as singer

definitions.meaning: a statement of charges for goods or work

explanation.surface: Bill is in good shape as a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name but is a statement of money owed; read as two words, the answer says a singer is in good voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader's itemised demand for payment, and a phrase meaning singing well, are the same letters.

clue.text: Norway's first, and only synthetic fabric

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word for the Scandinavian country is used
synthetic means artificially made up, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Norway leads the world in the one artificial textile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'synthetic' looks as if it describes the fabric, and the surface reads it that way, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters of 'only'.
explanation.definitionFit: The man-made polyamide fibre is woven into cloth for stockings and more.

clue.text: Love if rejected would make us annoyed

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the word for annoyed is read backwards

parts.note: someone annoyed is sore

explanation.surface: Love turned down would leave us cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue states it from the other side: the love god's name reversed makes SORE, so SORE reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, Cupid's counterpart, personifies desire.

clue.text: Wherein a clergyman lost one in York?

definitions.text: Wherein a clergyman lost one in York?

indicators.note: the clergyman's title has lost something, so a letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a minister is a member of the clergy
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A riddle about where some clergyman went missing in York.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I (one) from MINISTER. The whole clue also defines: York Minster is a great church where a clergyman might well be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cathedral-like church, York's being the most famous, is a place where clergy serve.

clue.text: Moody's aim in the theatre

definitions.meaning: Dwight L. Moody was an American evangelist whose goal was religious awakening
a new staging of an old play

explanation.surface: What a gloomy person hopes to achieve on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moody' looks like an adjective for a sulky person but is the nineteenth-century evangelist Dwight Moody, whose campaigns sought a religious reawakening.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist seeks a renewal of faith among the people, and a theatre company restages an older production.

clue.text: A group noted for striking sounds

definitions.text: A group noted for striking sounds

parts.words: A group noted for striking sounds
parts.note: the section of an orchestra, written in musical notes, whose instruments make their sound by being hit

explanation.surface: A band famous for its remarkable sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' seems to mean famous and 'striking' remarkable, but the group is one with written musical notes, and its sounds come from striking drums and cymbals.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestral section of drums, cymbals and similar instruments is played by hitting them.

clue.text: Shabby-sounding bearing

indicators.note: tells us the word for shabby is only heard, and a different spelling goes in the grid

parts.note: mean in the sense of poor or shabby, as in a mean dwelling

explanation.surface: A rather down-at-heel deportment.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's demeanour or carriage is their manner of holding themselves.

clue.text: Standing order from the office suppliers, say?

indicators.note: say tells us the word is spoken, and a similar-sounding spelling goes in the grid

parts.note: paper, envelopes and pens ordered from a stationer

explanation.surface: A regular order placed with the firm supplying office goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing order' looks like a regular payment, but 'Standing' alone is the definition. Paper goods (with an E) sound the same as the answer (with an A).
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing still is not moving.

clue.text: Bird is in no way well off

parts.note: O is a nought, nothing
ST is short for street, a way
wealthy people are rich

explanation.surface: Some bird is decidedly not prosperous.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flightless African runner is a species of bird.

clue.text: Sunshine workers who seize their opportunity

definitions.text: Sunshine workers who seize their opportunity

parts.words: Sunshine workers who seize their opportunity
parts.note: farm workers who cut grass in fine weather, following the proverb about making use of the sun while it shines

explanation.surface: Opportunists who work while the weather is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'make hay while the sun shines' means seize your chance; the farm labourers who literally do it are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmhands who cut and dry grass for fodder must work during dry weather.

clue.text: Strange new part of Belgium

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of the following words are made unfamiliar by rearranging

explanation.surface: An odd, newly built district somewhere in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges NEW PART; the whole clue then points to a part of Belgium, the port city of Flanders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish port city lies in northern Belgium.

clue.text: Miss Peachum, we hear, in sea disaster in the Pacific

indicators.note: we hear tells us the name is only spoken, and the shorter spelling goes in

parts.note: Polly Peachum is the heroine of Gay's The Beggar's Opera

indicators.note: disaster wrecks the order of the letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A character from The Beggar's Opera caught in a shipwreck in the Pacific Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Polly Peachum is the heroine of John Gay's eighteenth-century The Beggar's Opera; 'we hear' gives only the sound of her name, and 'disaster' rearranges 'in sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: The great island group of the central and southern ocean lies in that ocean.

clue.text: In capitals he is at home here

definitions.text: In capitals he is at home here

parts.words: In capitals he is at home here
parts.note: HE in capital letters stands for His Excellency, an ambassador, whose official residence abroad is meant

explanation.surface: A man feels comfortable living in big cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In capitals' seems to mean in capital cities (true enough), but it also says write HE in capital letters: His Excellency, the title of an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambassador's official mission and residence in a foreign capital is where His Excellency lives and works.

clue.text: Leading actress about to blossom — some bird!

indicators.note: the bud is placed about the star, around her

parts.note: a bud is a flower about to open
the leading lady of a show is its star

explanation.surface: A top actress is on the verge of flourishing, and what a woman she is!
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to blossom' reads as on the verge of flowering, but 'about' is the container signal and 'to' a link. 'Bird' is also British slang for a young woman, which fits the actress.
explanation.definitionFit: The great bustard is a large heavy ground-dwelling game bird of open plains.

clue.text: One of those 'carried by students at Chelsea

indicators.note: the answer is borne inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Something students in a London district carry around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'One of those' leans on the whole sentence: the bag is the very thing students carry, and it sits inside 'studentS AT CHELsea'. Chelsea is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag with a shoulder strap is what pupils carry their books in.

clue.text: Atrocious upset in House

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the following words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Something appalling stirs up trouble in the House of Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicked, shocking crime is utterly abominable.

clue.text: Writing about outsize cryptogam

indicators.note: the writing goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: An essay on an oversized spore-bearing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: A cryptogam is a plant that reproduces by spores rather than seeds, such as ferns, mosses and algae.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosses reproduce by spores, not flowers or seeds, which makes them a classic example of that plant group.

clue.text: A month in the borderland

definitions.meaning: the third month of the year
a frontier region, as in the Welsh or Scottish border areas

explanation.surface: Spending a month in the frontier country.
explanation.definitionFit: The third calendar month shares its name with an old word for a frontier territory, as in the Welsh Marches.

clue.text: A nice lad no unruly Sassenach!

definitions.text: A nice lad no unruly Sassenach!

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant boy who is certainly no rowdy Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sassenach is the Scots word for an English person, so the whole sentence describes a Scot, which is what the rearranged letters spell.
explanation.definitionFit: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a native of it is a Scot and by definition not English.

clue.text: It's currently of limited circulation

parts.note: a small swirl in a current of water, going round in a little circle, while seeming to describe a publication with few readers

explanation.surface: This item is presently printed in small numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currently' seems to mean now and 'circulation' readership; read literally, a current whose water circulates in a small area.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool-like swirl of water or air turns against the main flow.

clue.text: His progeny part of this celebrity's pride?

definitions.text: His progeny part of this celebrity's pride?

parts.words: His progeny part of this celebrity's pride?
parts.note: a celebrity can be called by this big-cat word, and a family group of those cats is a pride, so his cubs belong to it

explanation.surface: Is a famous man proud of his children?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like a parent's satisfaction, but it is the collective name for a group of big cats; a celebrity is also called by the big cat's name, as in a social lion.
explanation.definitionFit: A much-feted celebrity is the social big cat, and the king of beasts lives in a pride with his cubs.

clue.text: Understand about Eliza's transformation

parts.note: RE is Latin for concerning or about

indicators.note: transformation changes the shape of the name, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Grasping what Eliza Doolittle's makeover in Pygmalion was about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Eliza Doolittle, transformed in Shaw's Pygmalion; here 'transformation' rearranges only the letters of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to grasp or comprehend something is to become aware of it.

clue.text: These churchmen, lacking company, would gain promotion

indicators.note: the clue runs backwards: the promoted rank would gain the company to become these churchmen, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: deans rank above these clergy, so becoming deans is promotion
the company the churchmen are missing; CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Junior clergy without companions might rise up the church hierarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: The logic is reversed: these clergy without CO (company) leave a higher church rank, so the answer is that rank with the company abbreviation placed inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: These ordained ministers rank below priests and help with church services.

clue.text: Eastern fellow in this resort, a lover of pleasure

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the rearranged letters
read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: An oriental man staying at this holiday spot is a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort, a rearranging signal; 'in' then puts the eastern fellow inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives for enjoyment and sensual gratification follows the philosophy of pleasure as the highest good.

clue.text: She a heroine? Yes. Shaw? Mostly

parts.note: aye is an old or dialect word for yes

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the name, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A quiz about whether a famous female character was created by Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is H. Rider Haggard's novel, whose heroine is She-who-must-be-obeyed. AYE (yes) plus SHAW less its W builds her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard's immortal queen in the novel She is called by this name.
